title: When someone mocks
hook: responding to mockery of the turban with calm and courage
tomorrow: next summer's camp form came. will Simran come back from college?

segments.voice: Yesterday, on the bus: their own sikhi, found by keeping and by asking. Today Simran finds out how fiercely she keeps it for someone else.

Hot face. Tight jaw. Hands that want to do something. Simran is still feeling all three at pickup, telling Bebe what happened at lunch. Gurveer wore his new turban to school for the first time. A boy at the next table called it a tomato, reached over to flick it, and half the table laughed. Simran has seen this before, with Fateh's patka, and this time she wants to go back in and flip that table. Bebe puts a hand on her arm and says a line from Baba Farid instead.
screen: `HOT FACE. TIGHT JAW.` → `"THEY CALLED IT A TOMATO."` → `BEBE'S HAND ON HER ARM.`

segments.voice: Farid's salok, on ang 1381, says, in paraphrase: answer evil with goodness, and don't let anger fill your mind; then your body won't fall sick. Notice he starts with the body. The heat Simran feels is real, and Farid's point is that anger left to run will make you ill before it fixes anything. But calm isn't the same as doing nothing. Guru Tegh Bahadur's salok on ang 1427 gives the other half. In paraphrase: the one who frightens no one, and is afraid of no one, call that one wise. Two parts, held together. Don't frighten anyone: no flipped tables, no threats back. Don't be afraid: Gurveer doesn't have to take the turban off, or laugh along as if it's nothing. So that evening, on a call, they practice. Gurveer sits up, breathes out, and says in an ordinary voice: it's my dastar. I tied it myself this morning. That's calm courage, out loud. And Simran does her part the same way: the next day she goes with him to the school counselor, firm and unhurried. If teasing turns to pushing or threats, the adults step in. Calm courage never means putting up with harm.
screen: `FARID: ANGER MAKES THE BODY SICK.` · `CALM IS NOT DOING NOTHING.` · `FRIGHTEN NO ONE. FEAR NO ONE.` · `"IT'S MY DASTAR. I TIED IT."` · then, large: `CALM COURAGE.`

segments.voice: Sit tall with both feet flat on the floor. Unclench your jaw, drop your shoulders, and rest one hand on your chest. Breathe out slowly, longer than you breathe in, and feel the heat settle without letting your back slump.
When someone mocks. Answering with a steady body and a clear voice: frightening no one, afraid of no one.
Calm courage: the jaw unclenched, the voice clear, and the turban still on. See you tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 1649 COUNTS.` → `LIVING IT · 23 OF 134.` → `TOMORROW: NEXT SUMMER'S CAMP FORM. WILL SIMRAN COME BACK?`

howItsDone: Sikh families teach young people to answer mockery of the turban or patka calmly and plainly, to explain what it is, and to tell a trusted adult; parents and older siblings speak to schools when it continues.

fork.setup: a coworker keeps making jokes about your accent in meetings. going by today, what's the move?
options: laugh along so it looks like it doesn't bother you.
snap back in front of everyone so they never try it again.
steady your breath, then say plainly, without heat, that it isn't okay.
fork.reveal: frighten no one, fear no one: no counterattack, no hiding. a steady body first, then a clear voice.

original.note: Gurmukhi: nirbhau, without fear; a word from the Mool Mantar describing God.

chat.meaning: Calm courage frightens no one, including a shaken friend, and fears no one. He can get there at his own pace.
